lines.text: Is your Brita actually cleaning your water or just making it taste better?
His tap water reads 259 parts per million of dissolved stuff.
Then he builds a filter from a bottle with sand and charcoal for five bucks and it drops to 237.
And the 28 dollar Brita lands at 234 which is basically the same as the five dollar bottle.
That's because a Brita is mostly activated carbon which grabs chlorine and bad taste but lets dissolved minerals slide right through.
beats: ai:tiny white mineral grains slipping between black charcoal granules in clear water macro

lines.text: And the 300 dollar Berkey reads higher than tap water at 284 although that's common when the filters are new.
But the 29 dollar ZeroWater hits zero.
Because it uses ion exchange beads that swap every dissolved mineral for the ingredients of pure water.
beats: ai:macro of tiny amber resin beads with clear water flowing over them

lines.text: But a high number doesn't mean your water is unsafe because a lot of it is just calcium and magnesium.
beats: ai:a calm glass of sparkling mineral water on a stone table in soft light
ai:macro of white calcium mineral crystals in a glass of water
